back_translation: This is what the LORD says: Behold, I will rouse up the spirit of a destroyer against Babylon and against the people of Leb-kamai.
And I will send foreigners to Babylon to winnow her and empty her land, for on the day of disaster they will come against her from every side.
Do not let the archer bend his bow, and do not let him put on his armor; do not spare her young men; devote all her army to destruction.
They will fall slain in the land of the Chaldeans, pierced through in her streets.
For Israel and Judah have not been abandoned by their God, by the LORD of Hosts, even though their land is full of guilt against the Holy One of Israel.
Flee from the midst of Babylon; let each one save his own life; do not be destroyed because of her iniquity, for this is the time of the LORD's vengeance; he will repay her what she deserves.
Babylon was a gold cup in the hand of the LORD, making the whole earth drunk; the nations drank her wine, therefore they have gone mad.
Suddenly Babylon fell and was shattered; wail and mourn for her; bring balm and apply it to her pain, perhaps she may be healed.
We tried to heal Babylon, but she was not healed; abandon her, and let each of us go back to his own land, for her judgment reaches up to the heavens and rises to the clouds.
The LORD has brought forth our righteousness; come, let us proclaim in Zion what the LORD our God has done.

Sharpen the arrows; fill the quivers full; the LORD has roused the spirit of the kings of the Medes, for his plan is aimed against Babylon to destroy her, for this is the vengeance of the LORD, the vengeance for his temple.
Raise a banner against the walls of Babylon; reinforce the guard; station the watchmen; prepare the ambushers; for the LORD has both devised and done what he spoke against the people of Babylon.
You who dwell beside many waters, rich in treasures, your end has come, the thread of your life is cut.
The LORD of Hosts has sworn by himself: Surely I will fill you with men like a swarm of locusts, and they will shout in triumph over you.
The LORD who made the earth by his power, who established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
When his voice resounds, the waters in the heavens roar; he makes the clouds rise from the ends of the earth; he makes lightning with the rain and brings forth the wind from his storehouses.
Everyone is stupid and without knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his idol, for his cast image is a lie, and there is no breath in them.
They are worthless, a work to be laughed at; in the time of their punishment they will perish.
The Portion of Jacob is not like these, for he is the Maker of all things, and is the tribe of his inheritance; the LORD of Hosts is his name.
You are my war club, my weapon for battle; with you I shatter nations, with you I destroy kingdoms.
With you I shatter the horse and its rider, with you I shatter the chariot and its driver.
With you I shatter man and woman, with you I shatter old man and child, with you I shatter young man and young woman.
With you I shatter the shepherd and his flock, with you I shatter the farmer and his oxen, with you I shatter governors and officials.
The LORD says: I will repay Babylon and all the inhabitants of Chaldea before your very eyes for all the evil they have done in Zion.

The LORD says: Behold, O destroying mountain, I am against you, you who destroy the whole earth; I will stretch out my hand against you, and roll you down from the cliffs, and make you a burned mountain.
No one will take from you a cornerstone or a foundation stone, for you will be a perpetual desolation, declares the LORD.

Raise a banner in the land; blow the horn among the nations; prepare the nations against her; summon the kingdoms against her—Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz; appoint a commander against her; bring up horses like a swarm of locusts.
Prepare the nations against her—the kings of the Medes, with their governors and all their officials, and every land under their rule.
The earth quakes and writhes, for the plans of the LORD against Babylon stand firm, to make the land of Babylon a desolation, without inhabitant.
The warriors of Babylon have stopped fighting; they sit in the strongholds; their strength has dried up; they have become like women; her houses are burned, the bars of her gates are broken.
One courier runs to meet another, and one messenger follows another, to report to the king of Babylon that his city has been captured on every side.
The river fords have been seized, the marshes burned with fire, and the soldiers are terrified.
For this is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says: The Daughter of Babylon is like a threshing floor at the time it is trampled; in just a little while her harvest time will come.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon has devoured me, has crushed me, has set me aside like an empty vessel, has swallowed me like a monster, filled his belly with my delicacies, and then vomited me out.
The inhabitant of Zion will say, May the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon; and Jerusalem will say, May my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea.
Therefore this is what the LORD says: Behold, I will plead your cause and take vengeance for you; I will dry up her sea and make her springs run dry.
Babylon will become a heap of ruins, a haunt of jackals, an object of horror and scorn, without inhabitant.
They will roar together like young lions; they will growl like lion cubs.
While they are heated, I will set out a feast for them and make them drunk, so that they may revel, then they will sleep a perpetual sleep and never wake up, declares the LORD.
I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, like rams together with male goats.
How Sheshach has been captured! The city that was the praise of the whole earth has been seized! How Babylon has become a horror among the nations!
The sea has come up over Babylon; she is covered with its roaring waves.
Her cities have become a desolation, a dry and barren land, a land where no one lives and no son of man passes through.
I will punish Bel in Babylon, and make him spew out what he has swallowed; the nations will no longer stream to him; even the wall of Babylon will fall.
Come out from her midst, my people; let each one save his life from the fierce anger of the LORD.

Do not let your heart grow faint, and do not be afraid at the rumor heard in the land, for a rumor will come one year, and another rumor the next year; there will be violence in the land, and ruler against ruler.
Therefore behold, the days are coming when I will punish the idols of Babylon; her whole land will be put to shame, and all her slain will fall within her.
Then the heavens and the earth and all that is in them will shout for joy over Babylon, for the destroyers from the north will come against her, declares the LORD.
Babylon must fall for the slain of Israel, just as the slain of all the earth have fallen because of Babylon.
You who have escaped the sword, go and do not linger; remember the LORD from far away, and let Jerusalem come into your heart.
We are ashamed because we have heard reproach; disgrace has covered our faces, because foreigners have entered the holy places of the house of the LORD.
Therefore behold, the days are coming, declares the LORD, when I will punish her idols, and throughout her land the wounded will groan.
Even if Babylon ascends to the heavens and fortifies her lofty stronghold, the destroyers I send will come against her, declares the LORD.
A sound of crying comes from Babylon, the sound of great destruction from the land of the Chaldeans.
For the LORD is destroying Babylon and will silence her loud voice; their waves will roar like many waters; the tumult of their voice will resound.
For a destroyer is coming against her, against Babylon; her warriors will be captured, their bows will be broken, for the LORD is a God of retribution; he will repay in full.

I will make her princes, her wise men, her governors, her officials, and her warriors drunk; then they will sleep a perpetual sleep and never wake up, declares the King whose name is the LORD of Hosts.

This is what the LORD of Hosts says: The thick walls of Babylon will be leveled flat, and her high gates will be burned with fire; so the labor of the peoples will be for nothing, and the nations will exhaust themselves only for the fire, and grow weary.

This is the word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign; Seraiah was the quartermaster.
Jeremiah had written all the disaster that would come upon Babylon on a single scroll—all these words written concerning Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah, When you reach Babylon, see that you read aloud all these words,
and then say, O LORD, you have spoken concerning this place that you would cut it off so that no one will dwell in it, neither man nor beast, but it will be a perpetual desolation.
And when you have finished reading this scroll, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
and then say, In the same way Babylon will sink and not rise again, because of the disaster I will bring upon her, and they will grow weary. Here end the words of Jeremiah.
